narrative: Markets are grappling with resilient US labor data after October nonfarm payrolls surged to 165k versus 70k expected, pushing unemployment to 4.1% and raising December Fed rate hike odds to 76%. Strong data and lingering inflation are driving yields higher and cementing a higher-for-longer policy path. Equities suffered a severe tech-led selloff, with the Nasdaq sliding 5% on the week despite a modest Friday bounce, as systematic fund selling hit semiconductors and investors scrutinized AI capital discipline. Brent crude plummeted 14% across the week in its steepest drop since April 2020 amid shifting energy infrastructure risks and geopolitical developments. Meanwhile, post-midterm legislative gridlock is being digested as market-friendly, though budget shutdown deadlines and trade policy shifts remain key macro overhangs.

Nasdaq.why: Suffered its worst weekly drop since June (-5%) amid heavy AI valuation re-pricing and a 12% slide in the SOX index, though Amanda Agati notes the secular innovation cycle remains early despite the systematic unwind.

S&P 500.why: Anchors note the index rebounded 0.31% on Friday but had its worst week since June, balanced against strong Q3 earnings growth tracking above 30% and historical post-midterm 12-month gains.
